title: EEPROM Fault
shortDescription: Main control has lost or corrupted its configuration.
fullDescription:
Beko refrigerators post E0 when the EEPROM self-check fails. The fridge falls back to a default duty cycle and cannot accept setpoint changes.

A service-mode reload sometimes clears it; otherwise the control board must be replaced.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Technician reloads config or replaces board.

faq.a: Yes, default runtime keeps food cold.

title: Fresh Food Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The fresh food NTC is out of range.
fullDescription:
E1 indicates the fridge compartment sensor reads open or shorted. The fridge reverts to default cycling.

Replacement is usually accessible behind a cover on the rear wall.

title: Freezer Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer NTC reads out of range.
fullDescription:
E2 means the freezer sensor is open or shorted. The freezer continues under a default cycle but temperature accuracy is compromised.

Replace the NTC behind the rear freezer wall.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Access rear freezer wall, swap NTC.

faq.a: Yes, if the freezer warms noticeably.

title: Defrost Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Defrost termination sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E3 is raised when the evaporator defrost sensor reads open or shorted. Defrost becomes unreliable, leading to ice buildup.

Replace the sensor, typically clipped to the evaporator tube.

title: Defrost Heater Fault
fullDescription:
E4 indicates no current through the defrost heater. Open heater, blown thermal fuse, or open bimetal are typical causes.

Ice build-up follows quickly until repaired.
whenToCallPro: If harness is hard to reach.

title: Evaporator Fan Fault
shortDescription: Evaporator fan not at target speed.
fullDescription:
E5 is posted when the fan tacho is missing or slow. Ice on the blade, seized motor, or pinched harness cause it.

Defrost first, replace motor if needed.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Swap fan motor if fault persists.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Main and display boards are not communicating.
fullDescription:
E6 is posted when the serial link between boards drops. Loose hinge harness or failed board cause it.

Power cycle and reseat harness.

title: Damper Fault
shortDescription: Air damper motor is not at commanded position.
fullDescription:
E7 indicates the damper stepper motor does not confirm position. Iced damper or failed motor cause it.

Defrost often frees it; otherwise replace the damper.

title: Condenser Fan Fault
shortDescription: Condenser fan not at target speed.
fullDescription:
E8 indicates the condenser fan tacho is missing or slow. Dust, bent blade, or failed motor cause it.

Vacuum condenser and inspect fan.

title: Compressor Fault
shortDescription: Inverter compressor reports a run fault.
fullDescription:
E9 is posted when the inverter cannot start or keep the compressor running. Low voltage, locked rotor, or failed inverter cause it.

Replace inverter first; sealed system only if board is fine.

title: High Temperature Alarm
fullDescription:
HE is raised when the fridge or freezer has been above its safe threshold for a sustained period. Recent door opening, large food load, or hardware fault cause it.

Check door and allow several hours to pull back down.
whenToCallPro: If HE persists after 12 hours of normal operation.

faq.a: Discard perishables that were above 5 °C for 2+ hours.

title: Low Temperature Alarm
shortDescription: Interior is colder than setpoint range.
fullDescription:
LE is displayed when the fridge drops well below the setpoint, often because the damper is stuck open or the thermistor has drifted.

Power cycle and inspect the damper and NTC readings.
whenToCallPro: If compressor will not cycle off after sensor replacement.

faq.a: Yes but fresh produce may freeze.
